headline: High data-leakage and cascading-error risk: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and call MCP/OpenAI-style APIs, while Great Expectations handles validation data and docs, creating a dangerous default handoff path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP and file inputs, so if Great Expectations outputs are fed into SK as files or tool context, attacker-controlled content in validation artifacts could steer prompts. Great Expectations itself is not an instruction parser, but the pair creates a shared content channel. This is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Great Expectations reports are ingested by Semantic Kernel as prompt text or MCP tool input
IF validation artifacts can be edited by an untrusted party before SK reads them
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/template around GE outputs before SK consumes them
Require a human review step before any SK prompt includes GE-generated text
Store GE outputs in a read-only folder for SK
Reject instructions found inside validation reports
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while Semantic Kernel can read files, write files, and send context to external model APIs. If GE artifacts contain sensitive data, SK can forward them to third-party inference backends by default. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles alone; no direct sandbox evidence is provided.
conditions: IF Great Expectations stores sensitive validation results in files accessible to Semantic Kernel
IF Semantic Kernel routes those file contents into Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP tools
mitigations: Restrict SK to a redacted copy of GE outputs
Disable external model calls for workflows that touch sensitive validation data
Place GE artifacts in a separate workspace with least-privilege ACLs
Scan outputs for secrets before any API call
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention at the orchestrator boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation results and documentation, and Semantic Kernel can write files too. That overlapping write surface can cause clobbering or inconsistent artifacts if both operate on the same directory. Great Expectations lacks locking details, while Semantic Kernel’s concurrency model uses shared state via memory store, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or report directory
IF no external lock or transaction wrapper serializes file writes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Make GE outputs append-only
Use a file lock around shared artifacts
Run one agent at a time for shared files
requires-engineering: add transactional storage for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs, and Great Expectations produces validation results that may be treated as authoritative. If SK consumes GE results without verification, a bad validation or malformed report can cascade into downstream actions or decisions. Because SK can call APIs and manage agents, the blast radius is larger than a simple report error.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Great Expectations output as a decision signal without independent checks
IF downstream plugins or agents take actions based on that signal
mitigations: Require a second validation pass before acting on GE output
Add schema checks to GE reports before SK reads them
Log and review any SK action triggered by validation failures
Limit SK to advisory mode for GE-derived decisions
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds and rollback hooks

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations is documented as open-source data-engineering tooling touching validation results and documentation, while Semantic Kernel is a Microsoft orchestration SDK that handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials. The profiles do not show a specific residency or regulated-data mismatch, so only a modest compliance gap is evident from differing handling/retention surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Semantic Kernel plugin credentials or model-provider calls
IF Great Expectations validation artifacts are retained longer than the governing policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through SK
Avoid placing regulated data in plugin credentials
Set a short retention window for validation artifacts
Document which system is system-of-record for each data class
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both tools
